title: The Skeleton and Muscles
seo_title: Year 7 Science: Skeleton and Muscles Worksheets (Joints and Antagonistic Muscles)
standard_code: KS3 Biology: Skeletal and muscular systems
standard_text: The structure and functions of the human skeleton, to include support, protection, movement and making blood cells; biomechanics: the interaction between skeleton and muscles, including the measurement of force exerted by different muscles; the function of muscles and examples of antagonistic muscles.
meta_desc: Free Year 7 science worksheets on the skeleton and muscles: functions of the skeleton, joints, cartilage, ligaments and tendons, antagonistic muscles and measuring muscle forces. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Support, protect, move, make blood cells.
key_sub: Antagonistic muscles work in pairs: one contracts while the other relaxes.
body_html:
How to think about it

The skeleton supports, protects, helps us move and makes blood cells.

  • Joints let bones move: hinge joints (elbow, knee), ball and socket joints (hip, shoulder), fixed joints (skull).
  • Cartilage cushions, ligaments join bone to bone, tendons join muscle to bone.
  • Antagonistic muscles work in pairs: when one contracts, the other relaxes.
Example

Shoulder joint type?

Moves in almost every direction

Answer: ball and socket

Example

Biceps contract. Triceps?

Antagonistic pair

Answer: relax

Common mistakes

  • Thinking muscles push bones.
  • Thinking ligaments join muscle to bone.
  • Thinking bones are not living tissue.

faq.q: What is the difference between a ligament and a tendon?
faq.a: Ligaments join bone to bone at a joint. Tendons join muscle to bone.
